summary_en.motivation: This review aims to consolidate the criteria, advances, and challenges in 3D bioprinting specifically for lung and tracheal tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: A systematic literature survey was conducted to evaluate bioink properties, scaffold design, and printing parameters relevant to respiratory tissue constructs.
summary_en.result: Key challenges such as achieving vascularization and functional maturation were identified, along with future directions including multi-material printing and in situ bioprinting.
summary_en.validation: As a review paper, no experimental validation is provided; it synthesizes existing findings from the literature.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of dental root-analogue implant with desired properties
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) was used to process commercially pure titanium (Grade 1 ELI CP Ti) dental root-analogue implant (RAI) with oval cross-section abutment (OCSA) design. The RAI was tested with a fatigue test system according to ISO 14801, maximum compression load is 350 N, 450 N and 500 N, the load tilt angle is 30°, R = 0.1. To simulate the stress distribution of implant and alveolar bone, a finite-element model was established. The elastic modulus of implant materials was set to 90 GPa and 110 GPa to simulate CP Ti and Ti-6Al-4V, respectively. 300 N vertical or 300 N vertical/50 N horizontal occlusal loading was applied. The biomechanical behaviour of peri-implant bone was recorded. Fatigue strength of RAI sample was 500 N. The simulation results showed that at 300 N vertical loading or 300 N vertical/50 N horizontal loading, compared with Ti-6Al-4V, CP Ti had lower von Mises stress on implant and abutment which reduces the risk of failure compared to their respective strength levels; meanwhile, higher von Mises stress on alveolar bone reduces stress shielding. The study underscores that the CP Ti and SLM are favourable for the fabrication of RAI.

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate a dental root-analogue implant with desired mechanical properties using additive manufacturing.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting (SLM) of CP Ti was used to produce the implant, followed by fatigue testing according to ISO 14801 and finite element analysis of stress distribution in implant and bone.
summary_en.result: The CP Ti implant survived 500 N fatigue load and exhibited lower stress shielding compared to Ti-6Al-4V due to higher stress transferred to alveolar bone.
summary_en.validation: Fatigue testing with multiple load levels and finite element simulation validated the biomechanical performance.

papers.title: Development of a Platelet Lysate–Based Printable, Transparent Biomaterial With Regenerative Potential for Epithelial Corneal Injuries
papers.abstract: Purpose: To develop a human platelet lysate (hPL)-based bioink that is transparent and also encompasses the regenerative properties of hPL to facilitate wound healing. Methods: The effect of different batches of hPLand fetal bovine serum (FBS) on corneal epithelial cell growth and scratch assay was first examined using Incucyte Zoom. Various combinations of human fibrinogen (concentration range from 0.2 to 5 mg/mL) and thrombin (concentration from 1 to 10 U/mL) were combined with hPL to generate nine types of potential bioink. Rheology, transparency, and cell compatibility of bioinks were assessed and compared. The final selected bioink was used in an ex vivo corneal model to examine its ability in re-epithelization. Results: No significant difference was detected in cell proliferation and wound healing tests between different hPL batches at the same concentration. Scratch assay data showed that hPL had significantly higher effect on wound healing than FBS. Comparing across the nine bioinks, bioink 5 consisting of 10% hPL, 2 mg/mL fibrinogen, and 5 U/mL thrombin demonstrated all required mechanical and cellular properties and was able to regenerate the full-thickness epithelium ex vivo Conclusions: The results showed that a transparent and adhesive bioink can be generated by combining hPL, fibrinogen, and thrombin together. The bioink can be directly applied to a human cornea to promote corneal re-epithelization with huge potential applications in corneal injuries. Translational Relevance: The developed transparent hPL-based ink with its adhesive and healing ability showed that it could be used as a new treatment option for corneal injuries.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种透明、具有再生能力的血小板裂解液基生物墨水用于角膜上皮损伤修复。
summary_zh.method: 通过组合不同浓度的人纤维蛋白原和凝血酶与血小板裂解液制备九种生物墨水，评估流变、透明度和细胞相容性，并选择最佳墨水在离体角膜模型上测试。
summary_zh.result: 筛选出的生物墨水5（10%hPL, 2mg/mL纤维蛋白原, 5U/mL凝血酶）具有所需性能，能促进全厚角膜上皮再生。
summary_zh.validation: 离体角膜模型上皮再生的组织学评估。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a transparent bioink with regenerative properties from human platelet lysate for treating corneal epithelial injuries.
summary_en.method: Nine bioink formulations were prepared by varying concentrations of human fibrinogen and thrombin combined with platelet lysate, and the optimal formulation was selected based on rheology, transparency, and cytocompatibility for ex vivo testing.
summary_en.result: The selected bioink (10% hPL, 2 mg/mL fibrinogen, 5 U/mL thrombin) supported full-thickness corneal epithelial regeneration ex vivo.
summary_en.validation: Ex vivo corneal wound healing model with histological assessment of re-epithelialization.
